sections.h2: Who collects property tax on a house inside Cleveland city limits?
sections.html:
A house inside Cleveland gets two separate tax bills, one from the City of Cleveland and one from Bradley County. The Bradley County Assessor of Property values the parcel for both governments. Payment of the county bill goes to the Bradley County Trustee, and payment of the city bill goes to the city's finance office.

  • City of Cleveland Finance: Municipal Building, 190 Church Street NE, open weekdays until 5 in the afternoon. Phone (423) 472-4551, and mail to P.O. Box 1519.
  • Bradley County Trustee: 1701 Keith Street NW, phone (423) 728-7247. Monday through Thursday it keeps 8:30 to 4:30, and Friday it stays open until 5. Tim Akins was elected Trustee in 2026.
  • Bradley County Assessor of Property: (423) 728-7126, for address changes, values and appeals.

The county also takes calls on its toll-free automated payment line at (833) 591-7276.

sections.h2: When do Cleveland tax bills come due and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Cleveland mails its bills during the first week of October. Payment is due from October 1, and no penalty applies through February 28 of the following year. If payment is not received or postmarked by February 28, a 1.5 percent charge is added on the first of March and again each month after that.

The city's own page says that charge keeps building to a cap of 18 percent, which takes twelve months. After that, unpaid taxes pass to the Bradley County Clerk and Master. The Trustee's page asks owners to pay county tax by the end of February as well.

sections.h2: What is the Cleveland and Bradley County tax rate?
sections.html:
The county's net rate for 2025 is .9922 on each $100 of assessed value. The Trustee's FAQ shows two fire district surcharges that apply only to county-only properties: .2182 inside the fire fringe and .2408 outside it, which would not apply to a house inside Cleveland.

The Trustee does not publish the city rate on its FAQ and directs owners to the city office at (423) 472-4551, so ask for the current Cleveland rate when estimating a bill. Tennessee assesses residential property at 25 percent of appraised value. For a house at $272,200, the Census Bureau's median owner-occupied value in Cleveland, that means $68,050 of assessed value, and the .9922 county rate turns it into roughly $675 of county tax before any city charge.

sections.h2: What relief exists for Cleveland homeowners who struggle with the bill?
sections.html:
Bradley County runs the state Tax Relief program through the Trustee's office, and it also runs its own Tax Freeze for owners 65 and older. The City Clerk's office can take state relief applications at the Municipal Building as well.

  • Tax Relief reimburses part of the tax for elderly or disabled owners who live in the home. For 2025 the county brochure listed up to $81 for Cleveland city residents, $99 inside the fire fringe and $101 outside it.
  • Tax Freeze was adopted by the Bradley County Commission in August 2007. It holds the tax at the amount for the first year the owner qualifies, as long as the owner stays eligible and makes no improvements.
  • Disabled veterans and surviving spouses can qualify for relief paid on the first $175,000 of home market value.

All taxes must be paid and current before relief is granted. The 2025 application deadline was April 5, 2026, so ask the Trustee for the 2026 deadline and income limit.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Cleveland property valuation?
sections.html:
Ring the county Assessor of Property at (423) 728-7126 and request an informal look at the value. The Assessor's appraisal staff look at the file first, and a disagreement can go to the Board of Equalization, a panel of local citizens.

The city's finance page notes that appeals can be started at any time but are heard in the spring, and a decision affects only that year's tax. The Tennessee Comptroller states that county boards usually convene on June 1 and that an appeal to the county board keeps the right to go on to the State Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: What happens if Cleveland property tax is never paid?
sections.html:
The Bradley County Clerk and Master runs the annual tax sale on delinquent parcels, and the Trustee's office does not keep a mailing list. The county says sales are open public auctions, the notice list is published two to three weeks before the sale, and the price is paid in cash, money order or check at the time of sale.

A sale clears every lien except state and federal liens. The buyer waits a year from the filing of the sale confirmation before taking possession, and the former owner may redeem in that window. The buyer earns 10 percent a year during the redemption period. Contact the Clerk and Master at (423) 728-7209 for the next sale.

sections.h2: What should a Cleveland seller know about the local housing stock?
sections.html:
Cleveland holds the Bradley County seat and is the county's biggest city. Its incorporation dates to February 4, 1842. The 2020 census counted 47,356 residents, and the Census Bureau estimated 51,172 for July 2025, living on about 27 square miles of land.

The terrain is a series of parallel ridges, including Candies Creek Ridge, that extend the Appalachians north to south. Interstate 75 passes through the west side with three exits, the APD-40 beltway circles the business district, and Paul Huff Parkway is a major road on the north side. Lee University and Cleveland State Community College both operate here. Cleveland City Schools educates students who live inside the city limits, and Bradley County Schools maintains some campuses within the city as well.

Manufacturing anchors the local economy. Employers named for the area include Whirlpool, Mars, Procter and Gamble and Duracell. Figures for 2020 to 2024 show 18,829 households, $58,559 in median household income and a 21.3 minute average commute. Owners occupy 48.0 percent of homes and renters pay a median $1,034, so a seller may well have a tenant in place.

sections.h2: How should a Cleveland seller deal with tax owed at closing?
sections.html:
The county advises new owners to study the closing statement and ask the title company who pays, since responsibility turns on the transfer date and unpaid tax keeps accruing against the property. Ask the title company to pull both the county and city tax status before the contract date.

Cleveland's online system lets anyone verify that the current tax is paid, and the city office can supply a duplicate bill at (423) 472-4551. City partial payment agreements and payment plans only work if the balance is cleared before March, so a seller on one of those plans should ask the title company for a payoff figure instead of assuming the remaining installments transfer.

faqs.q: When is Cleveland property tax due?
faqs.a: The city bill is due starting October 1, and February 28 is the last penalty-free day. A 1.5 percent monthly charge begins in March and stops growing at 18 percent.

faqs.q: Who do I pay for property tax in Cleveland, TN?
faqs.a: Pay the City of Cleveland for the city tax and the Bradley County Trustee for the county tax. The city finance office is at 190 Church Street NE and the Trustee is at 1701 Keith Street NW.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Cleveland property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. The city accepts partial payments if you complete forms and pay the whole amount before March 1, and it offers a twelve month plan if forms are in by February 15. Online card payments carry a 3 percent fee.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cleveland property value?
faqs.a: Start with the county Assessor at (423) 728-7126. If you still disagree after that review, the Board of Equalization takes the appeal in spring.

faqs.q: What if I leave a Cleveland property tax bill unpaid?
faqs.a: Interest climbs by 1.5 percent each month to a cap of 18 percent, and then the debt passes to the Bradley County Clerk and Master. Parcels still delinquent can go to a public auction, with one year to redeem.
